role.altitude: The QC analyst keeps sampling, testing, training at the bench and talking with other departments; retyping certificates, instrument results and contract-lab reports and building data tables by hand shrink.
skills_to_grow: Checking extracted values and generated tables against source records
role.ambitious_version: A QC analyst whose data reach production and regulatory affairs straight from the LIMS, with no retyping.

tasks.short: Receive the delivery notice, check the supplier certificate against the specification, sample and inspect raw materials, record results, compare with limits and have QA release or reject.

steps.what: Warehouse receives the raw material, puts it in quarantine and tells QC
QC analyst checks the supplier's certificate of analysis, labels and order against the specification

loop.input: The supplier's certificate of analysis as PDF and the material's specification in the LIMS.
loop.output: Certificate values per test parameter, with lot number and dates, compared with the specification limits by plain code.
loop.check: The analyst confirms every extracted value against the PDF field by field before it is saved; values the step cannot read are left empty for the analyst to type.
loop.why_not_simpler: Suppliers send certificates in their own layouts, so fixed field positions do not work.

steps.what: QC analyst receives and samples the raw materials in the sampling booth
QC analyst inspects the raw materials and runs identity tests
QC analyst writes the results in the logbook and types them into the LIMS
QC analyst compares results with the specification and proposes release or rejection
QA officer reviews the release proposal and approves release or rejection
QA officer changes the material status from quarantine to released or rejected in the warehouse system

approvals.approved_version: release decision for that lot as e-signed by QA in s7, with the result set it was based on; any later result change voids it

tasks.design: A goods receipt in the {OPS_SYSTEM} creates the sample request in the LIMS ({OTHER}). A bounded step reads the supplier's certificate PDF into fields that plain code compares with the specification, and the analyst confirms every value against the PDF. Identity and other instruments send their results straight to the LIMS, which compares them with the limits; sampling and testing stay with the analyst, QA e-signs the release, and only then does the material status change in the warehouse system.
tasks.previous_blocker: Certificates and instrument results were retyped, and limits were compared by eye.
tasks.enabler_now: LIMS connect to instruments and the warehouse system; language models read varied PDFs into fields that a person confirms.
tasks.still_hard: Sampling and judging an odd-looking material.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing a material that passes tests but is not right.
tasks.altitude: Less retyping; release decisions stay with QA.

reach.learn: Which suppliers' certificates differ most from QC results.

evidence.claim: A lab data product structures PDFs and contract-lab reports into data.
A LIMS barcodes samples, assigns tests and logs each change.
The draft GMP annex on AI bars generative AI from critical GMP decisions; computerised systems must be validated under the current annex.

assumptions: Boundary: from the delivery notice to the material status set; supplier qualification is outside.
Input contract for s2: certificates as PDF from suppliers, specifications in the LIMS kept by QC; fallback is typing.
Input contract for s5: identity and other instruments connected to the LIMS; about 70% of raw material tests run on connected instruments; s5 is priced at that share.
Release stays a QA decision; the extraction tool and interfaces are validated before use.
Sampling and testing keep their full time; warehouse and QA time are outside the analyst's savings.
unknowns: Deliveries per week and tests per material.
Which instruments can connect to the LIMS.
research_questions: How many extracted certificate values does the analyst correct?

already_counted.description: QC analyst confirms each extracted certificate value against the PDF.

incremental.description: QC analyst keeps specifications and certificate field mappings current and joins revalidation after changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few suppliers with tidy certificates and manual instruments; high: many suppliers and mostly connected instruments.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare training from the current SOP, demonstrate the procedure, supervise the trainee, assess competence, record the training and update the training matrix and system rights.

steps.what: QC analyst prepares training on laboratory procedures and assays from the current SOP

loop.output: A draft step checklist and short knowledge questions for the trainee.
loop.check: Every checklist item and question answer must cite an SOP section, or it is dropped; the analyst edits the material before use.
loop.why_not_simpler: The SOP is prose; turning it into a checklist and questions needs rewriting.

steps.what: QC analyst trains other analysts by demonstrating the procedure at the bench
QC analyst supervises the trainee running the assay
QC analyst assesses the trainee's competence from results and observation and signs the training record
QC analyst files the paper training record and enters it in the training system
QC lead updates the training matrix and gives the trainee the right to run the assay in the LIMS

approvals.approved_version: training record for that trainee, assay and SOP version as e-signed in s4; a new SOP version needs new training

tasks.design: A bounded step drafts a step checklist and knowledge questions from the current SOP, each citing its section, for the analyst to edit. Demonstrating, supervising and judging competence stay at the bench; the analyst e-signs the training record in the {LMS}, which links it to the SOP version, and the signed record grants the trainee the assay right in the LIMS instead of a manual matrix update.
tasks.previous_blocker: Training records were on paper and the matrix and LIMS rights were updated by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Learning systems link records to document versions and can feed user rights.
tasks.still_hard: Teaching the feel of a good technique.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing why a trainee's results drift.
tasks.altitude: Less paperwork; nothing changes at the bench.

reach.learn: Whether SOP-linked records close audit findings.

evidence.claim: Learning systems link training records to document versions and can update user rights in other systems.
GMP requires trained staff and records of training; computerised systems must be validated.

assumptions: Boundary: from preparing training to assay rights granted; writing SOPs is outside.
Input contract for s1: the current approved SOP from the document system; fallback is preparing by hand.
Demonstration, supervision and the competence judgement keep their full time; the QC lead's time is outside the analyst's savings.
research_questions: Do audits find fewer training gaps?

already_counted.description: QC analyst checks drafted checklists against the SOP.

incremental.description: QC analyst links new SOP versions to the training items.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: one long assay training a year; high: many short trainings after SOP changes.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Take the request from regulatory affairs, pull batch and stability results, compile the tables, verify them, write short summaries, get the package approved and supply the QC data for the regulatory submission.

steps.what: Regulatory affairs asks QC for data for a submission: specifications, batch analyses, stability
QC analyst finds batch and stability results in the LIMS and archives
QC analyst compiles batch analysis and stability tables in the submission format
QC analyst verifies the tables against the source records
QC analyst writes short summaries of results and trends

loop.input: The verified tables and the specification limits.
loop.output: Draft summary sentences on results against limits and trends over time.
loop.check: Every number must match a cell in the verified tables, or the sentence is marked; trend statements must match the computed trend; the analyst edits every sentence.
loop.why_not_simpler: Tables give the numbers; the submission needs a few sentences saying what they show.

steps.what: QC manager reviews and approves the final data package
QC analyst supplies the approved QC data package to regulatory affairs

approvals.approved_version: data package (tables and summary) as e-signed by the QC manager in s6; any change voids the approval

tasks.design: Validated LIMS ({OTHER}) queries pull batch and stability results by product and batch range, and a table generator fills the submission formats straight from them, so there is no retyping to check, only spot checks and data from older paper archives. A bounded step drafts summary sentences with every number checked against the tables, and the analyst edits them. The QC manager e-signs the final package and the document system passes exactly that version to regulatory affairs, who own the submission.
tasks.previous_blocker: Results were copied from LIMS screens and archives into spreadsheets and then verified line by line.
tasks.enabler_now: LIMS report tools and document generators produce validated tables from stored results.
tasks.still_hard: Data from old batches that never entered the LIMS.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which out-of-trend result will draw a regulator's question.
tasks.altitude: The analyst checks instead of copying; decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Compile the quality module of a submission
reach.learn: Whether generated tables cut questions back to QC.

evidence.claim: A LIMS generates certificates of analysis with e-signatures and audit trails.
A pharmaceutical company reported report writing time down 90% and verification protocol effort down 95% with model drafting and people approving (vendor case).
Computerised systems in GMP, including table generators, must be validated.

assumptions: Boundary: from the data request to the package supplied to regulatory affairs; the submission itself is outside.

Input contract for s2 and s3: results in the LIMS with product, batch, test, value, unit and date; about 75% of requested data is in the LIMS and the rest in paper archives; s2 to s4 are priced at that share.
The table generator is validated once per template; generated tables are spot-checked, archive data is verified in full.
Regulatory affairs and QC manager time are outside the analyst's savings.
unknowns: Submissions per year and their data volume.
How far back the LIMS holds data.
research_questions: How many questions from regulators trace to QC data errors?

already_counted.description: QC analyst spot-checks generated tables and verifies archive data in full.

incremental.description: QC analyst joins validation of the table generator after template or LIMS changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: an old product with most data in paper archives; high: a recent product with all batch and stability data in the LIMS.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Answer questions from production, QA and R&D, send samples to contract labs and enter their results, deal with vendors on instruments and supplies, and take part in cross-department meetings.

steps.what: QC analyst answers questions from production, QA and R&D on results, status and methods
QC analyst arranges sample shipments and test requests with contract labs
QC analyst enters results from contract lab reports into the LIMS

loop.input: The contract lab's report PDF and the test request in the LIMS.
loop.output: Result values per requested test with units and sample ids, ready to save in the LIMS.
loop.check: Sample ids must match the request; the analyst confirms every value against the PDF field by field before saving; unreadable values are typed by the analyst.
loop.why_not_simpler: Each contract lab uses its own report layout.

steps.what: QC analyst serves as technical liaison with vendors on instrument service and lab supplies
QC analyst takes part in meetings with other departments on deviations, investigations and changes

tasks.design: A test status view on the LIMS ({OTHER}) lets production and QA see which samples are tested, pending or out of limits, so fewer status questions reach the analyst. Sample shipments to contract labs use a request and chain-of-custody form generated from the LIMS, and a bounded step reads each contract lab report into result fields that the analyst confirms value by value. Vendor talks and cross-department meetings stay with the analyst.
tasks.previous_blocker: Status lived in the analyst's head and contract lab PDFs were retyped.
tasks.enabler_now: LIMS offer status views to other departments; language models read varied report PDFs into fields.
tasks.still_hard: Investigations where departments disagree on the cause.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining a test result so production acts on it.
tasks.altitude: Fewer status calls and less retyping; decision rights do not change.

reach.learn: Whether a status view cuts waiting for QC answers.

evidence.claim: A lab data product structures contract-lab reports into data.
Computerised systems used in GMP, including the extraction step, must be validated.

assumptions: Boundary: QC's exchanges with departments, contract labs and vendors; the investigations themselves are outside.
Input contract for s3: contract lab reports as PDF with the sample ids from the request; fallback is typing.
Coverage: about half of department questions are status questions the view answers; s1 is priced at that share.
Vendor talks and meetings keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of tests sent to contract labs.
research_questions: How many status questions remain after the view goes live?

already_counted.description: QC analyst confirms each extracted contract lab value against the PDF.

incremental.description: QC analyst keeps report field mappings per contract lab current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few outsourced tests and a production team that calls anyway; high: many contract lab reports and frequent status questions.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
